cards.title: What are Services?
cards.content:
Angular Services

Services are typically classes with a narrow, well-defined purpose. They are used to share data, logic, and functionality across multiple components, adhering to the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle.

In Angular, services are often injected into components using Dependency Injection (DI).

cards.title: The @Injectable Decorator
cards.content:
@Injectable Decorator

The @Injectable() decorator marks a class as available to be provided and injected as a dependency.

import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';

@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class DataService { }

Using providedIn: 'root' creates a single, shared instance (singleton) of the service that is available application-wide.

cards.title: Dependency Injection (DI)
cards.content:
Dependency Injection

DI is a design pattern in which a class requests dependencies from external sources rather than creating them. Angular's DI framework provides declared dependencies to a class when that class is instantiated.

constructor(private dataService: DataService) { }
